title: Spending policies: who and what can consume Copilot Credits, and up to how much
summary: Hold: the Graph update note says only four properties can be supplied, overlooking the billing target required when switching a policy to pay-as-you-go. Administrators following that restriction could submit an invalid billing change.

claims.claim: A spending policy is an administrator-defined rule in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Administrators use the Cost management dashboard in the Microsoft 365 admin center to govern access, establish spending controls, manage credit requests, and monitor consumption.

claims.claim: Policies govern access for users, groups, agents and environments.
claims.quote:
Control which users and groups can access supported services using identity-based policies.
- Set spending limits for supported users, environments, and agents.

claims.claim: A policy selects which agents and services can consume credits.
claims.quote: Use the check box to select the agents and services that can consume credits against the billing method tied to this policy.

claims.claim: Policies can set a monthly spending limit.
claims.quote: When you select a limited monthly budget, you limit the number of credits that this policy can spend each month.

claims.claim: Policies specify a billing method.
claims.quote: Select the billing method for a policy.

claims.where: What it is; Why it matters
claims.claim: Spending policies are limit-based controls.
claims.quote: Spending policies are limit-based controls and don't reserve or allocate Copilot Credits to users or groups.

claims.claim: A spending policy does not reserve credits.
claims.quote: Spending policies are limit-based controls and don't reserve or allocate Copilot Credits to users or groups.

claims.where: What it is; Governance controls: Interaction
claims.claim: A spending policy does not allocate credits.
claims.quote: Spending policies only define access and spending limits, not credit allocation.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: An identity-based policy follows the person using selected services.
claims.quote: Use this option when you want a policy to apply to the people who use selected agents and services.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: Identity policies can cover all users or specific groups.
claims.quote: By default, All users is selected. To target this rule to a subset of users, switch to Specific groups and select the directory group.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy; How it works
claims.claim: An identity policy offers an optional monthly per-user limit.
claims.quote: Select monthly budget limits for users (optional). Use the toggle to select this option and to set a monthly limit for users to prevent a single person from spending all available credits.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: An identity policy can govern a group using Cowork.
claims.quote: Use this option when you want a policy to apply to the people who use selected agents and services. For example, a group using Cowork.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: Copilot Studio resource policies follow the agent or environment rather than the person.
claims.quote: Use this option when you want usage to follow an agent or environment rather than the identity of the person using it.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: Resource policies can cover specific agents, specific environments or all environments.
claims.quote: Specific resources: Choose Specific resources when particular agents need their own policy or billing method.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy; controls[4]
claims.claim: Resource policies support per-agent limits.
claims.quote: You can also set a per-agent limit so that no single agent covered by the policy uses more than the amount you specify.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: An identity-based policy cannot be converted into a resource-based policy.
claims.quote: You can't convert an existing identity-based policy into a resource-based policy.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: The default setup targets the whole organisation and all users.
claims.quote: The default setup targets your entire organization and all users.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Activating the default policy unlocks experiences gated by usage-based billing.
claims.quote: This process activates AI experiences, like Cowork, that are gated by usage-based billing.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Each additional policy has an independent limit.
claims.quote: Each additional spending policy that you create has its own independent limit and doesn't inherit the tenant-level limit.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Additional policies do not inherit the tenant-level limit.
claims.quote: Each additional spending policy that you create has its own independent limit and doesn't inherit the tenant-level limit.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: A policy can hold alert thresholds.
claims.quote:
Configure policy-level alerts:

    - Specify the usage threshold for the policy.

claims.where: What it is: How it works; Risks and limits; What to check
claims.claim: Auto-apply new services is on by default.
claims.quote: By default, the Auto-apply new services toggle is selected for spending policies.

claims.where: What it is: How it works; Risks and limits; What to check
claims.claim: Auto-apply automatically adds future supported services and agents unless turned off.
claims.quote: When the setting is on, newly supported Microsoft Copilot services and agents are automatically added to the policy.

claims.where: What it is: How it works; What to check
claims.claim: For overlapping identity policies for the same service, the highest per-user limit wins first.
claims.quote:
If a user is in more than one policy for the same service, the system assigns the user a policy based on the following order:

1. Highest per-user limit

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Tied per-user limits are resolved by the largest overall policy limit.
claims.quote: If tied, the largest overall policy limit

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: A remaining tie is resolved by the most recently created policy.
claims.quote: If still tied, the most recently created policy

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: A missing per-user limit is replaced by the overall policy limit for the overlap comparison.
claims.quote: If a policy doesn't have a per-user limit set, the system uses its overall policy limit as the per-user value for this comparison.

claims.where: What it is: How it works; Risks and limits
claims.claim: The selected policy applies in full rather than combining limits or settings.
claims.quote: The chosen policy applies in full and settings from other policies aren't combined.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: A Microsoft 365 spending policy covering Copilot Studio usage takes precedence over Power Platform controls.
claims.quote: If a spending policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center covers the environment or agent, its controls take precedence over the Power Platform admin center controls for that usage.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: A Copilot Studio resource policy takes precedence over an identity policy.
claims.quote: Within the Microsoft 365 admin center, a policy for the agent or its environment takes precedence over a policy for the person using the agent.

claims.claim: Initial usage-based billing setup includes activating the default spending policy.
claims.quote: Before you create additional spending policies, complete the initial usage-based billing setup and activate the default spending policy.

claims.where: Why it matters; What to check
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends setting a per-user limit to prevent runaway spending by one person.
claims.quote: Although this selection is optional, review and set this option for your organization to prevent runaway spending of Copilot Credits by one individual user.

claims.claim: Don't limit monthly spending allows policy consumption without a policy-level ceiling.
claims.quote: Don't limit monthly spending - Allows the policy to use credits against the organization's billing method without restrictions.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio resource policies are opt-in and existing Power Platform configuration remains until adoption.
claims.quote: To opt in, create a Microsoft 365 admin center resource-based spending policy. Until then, your existing Power Platform admin center configuration remains in effect.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits; controls[4].note
claims.claim: Covered resources move to Microsoft 365 credit management instead of Power Platform capacity allocations.
claims.quote: For resources covered by the spending policy, Copilot Credit management moves to the Microsoft 365 admin center, replacing their Power Platform admin center capacity allocations and linked billing plans.

claims.claim: Linked Power Platform billing plans no longer apply to covered environments.
claims.quote: Existing Power Platform capacity allocations and linked billing plans don't apply while spending for that environment is managed by a resource-based spending policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: A spending policy is not a purchase; charges arise from consumed Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Microsoft's usage-based billing model charges customers based on actual usage, measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Consumed credits are billed to the subscription selected in the billing method.
claims.quote: Copilot credits are billed to the subscription that you select in the billing method.

claims.claim: When credits run out for the subscription selected as the billing method, usage continues on pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: Copilot credits are billed to the subscription that you select in the billing method. New policies use it by default. When credits run out for that subscription, usage automatically continues on a pay-as-you-go basis.

claims.claim: When both capacity packs and a subscription with P3 are selected, the billing order is packs, P3, then pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote:
If you select both Prepaid Capacity packs and an Azure subscription with Copilot Credit Pre-purchase plan (P3), billing is applied in the following order to keep spending predictable:

- Prepaid Capacity packs
- Copilot Credit Pre-purchase plan (P3)
- Pay-as-you-go billing

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance controls: Roles
claims.claim: Global and Billing administrators can override billing methods per policy for departmental billing.
claims.quote: If you're a Global administrator or a Billing administrator, you can override this selection and select how this policy should be billed. This feature enables you to do departmental billing and vary billing methods for each group, department, or set of users.

claims.claim: Cowork requires a Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Cowork (Copilot license required)

claims.claim: The spending-policy pages do not publish service credit rates and refer readers to the Copilot Credits Guide.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot spending policy Copilot Credits rates licensing price. Read setup, manage-credits, manage-Studio-costs, billing overview and monitoring pages in full; none lists service rates. Overview links to the Copilot Credits Guide.

claims.claim: Consumption displays an estimated cost that might not match the bill.
claims.quote: Cost: The estimated cost of your AI usage in local currency, including negotiated rates. It includes usage paid for with prepaid credits and with pay-as-you-go, so it might not match your bill.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Hitting a limit; Governance controls: Interaction
claims.claim: Reaching a spending limit blocks access to agents and services.
claims.quote: When users hit the limit, they lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month until credits reset on the first of the month.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Hitting a limit
claims.claim: The monthly reset occurs on the first of the month.
claims.quote: When users hit the limit, they lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month until credits reset on the first of the month.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Hitting a limit; Governance controls: Watching
claims.claim: Users reaching a limit can request more credits.
claims.quote: When users reach their limit within a policy, they can request more credits but they don't default to other policies.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Hitting a limit
claims.claim: Users do not fall back to another policy after reaching their assigned policy's limit.
claims.quote: The system keeps the user on the assigned policy and doesn't reevaluate the user against other policies.

claims.where: Risks and limits: A per-user overrun
claims.claim: A running task exceeding a per-user limit can finish uninterrupted.
claims.quote: If a running task exceeds the per-user limit, it can complete without interruption.

claims.where: Risks and limits: A per-user overrun
claims.claim: Excess usage from a running task does not count toward the policy limit.
claims.quote: The excess usage doesn't count toward the policy limit, isn't billed (at Microsoft's sole discretion), and doesn't appear as consumed credits in the Cost Management dashboards

claims.where: Risks and limits: A per-user overrun; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft describes this excess usage as not billed at its sole discretion.
claims.quote: The excess usage doesn't count toward the policy limit, isn't billed (at Microsoft's sole discretion), and doesn't appear as consumed credits in the Cost Management dashboards

claims.where: Risks and limits: A per-user overrun
claims.claim: That excess does not appear as consumed credits in Cost Management dashboards.
claims.quote: The excess usage doesn't count toward the policy limit, isn't billed (at Microsoft's sole discretion), and doesn't appear as consumed credits in the Cost Management dashboards

claims.where: Risks and limits: All environments; What to check
claims.claim: Selecting All environments transitions every environment in the tenant.
claims.quote: Selecting All environments makes this change for every environment in the tenant.

claims.where: Risks and limits: All environments; Open questions
claims.claim: A newly linked environment can take up to 12 minutes to apply the policy.
claims.quote: After you link an environment to a Microsoft 365 spending policy, allow up to 12 minutes for the new policy to apply.

claims.claim: Removing an environment or deleting its resource policy restores the applicable Power Platform policy.
claims.quote: If you remove an environment from a spending policy or delete the resource-based spending policy, the applicable Power Platform admin center policy resumes for that environment automatically.

claims.claim: Resource policies do not apply to AI Builder features or their credits.
claims.quote: Resource-based policies created in the Microsoft 365 admin center don't apply to AI Builder features or the credits they consume.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises against moving resources using AI Builder into resource policies.
claims.quote: Don't move resources, agents, workflows or environments that use AI Builder to these policies.

claims.claim: A user's previous consumption carries forward when group membership changes policies.
claims.quote: Credits consumed under the previous spending policy remain part of the user's consumption history and are accounted for when enforcing the spending limit under the new policy.

claims.claim: After a group move, Consumption shows only current-policy usage at user level.
claims.quote: Only the current usage against the current spending policy is displayed at a user level in the Consumption tab view.

claims.claim: Policy coverage is tied to the supported usage-based billing service list.
claims.quote: For a list of services managed by usage-based billing method, see Services managed by usage-based billing.

claims.claim: Microsoft says more services will be managed by this experience.
claims.quote: Microsoft is working to bring more agents and services to be managed by this experience.

claims.claim: The policy documentation directs Copilot Chat, SharePoint agents and Retrieval API readers to a separate pay-as-you-go page.
claims.quote: For Copilot Chat, SharePoint Agents, or Microsoft Copilot Retrieval API (Preview), see Microsoft Copilot pay-as-you-go service overview.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Default-policy setup opens at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Get Started.
claims.quote:
In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot and then the Cost Management node.
To unlock AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing, select Get Started.

claims.claim: No API is documented as equivalent to activating the initial default policy.
claims.quote: Searched: "default spending policy" activate Microsoft Graph allUsersSpendingPolicy. Read setup, Graph overview and create; read allUsersSpendingPolicy search excerpt. Creating an all-users policy is documented, but not equivalence to initial activation.

claims.claim: Initial activation uses the Global administrator or Billing administrator role.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center with one of the following administrator roles:

    - Global administrator
    - Billing administrator

claims.claim: Identity policy creation uses Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy > Identity.
claims.quote:
Select the Configuration tab and then select + Add spending policy.
Create and name the policy and then choose Identity as the scope.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies creates an identity policy with limits, services and a billing method.
claims.quote: Required properties are displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and serviceSettings. You can optionally supply billingMethods and billingInstrument.
claims.fix: Append 'Set billingMethods to select the funding method.' to controls[1].note and its rendered counterpart. The row governs billing method selection but currently names only the other deciding request properties.

claims.claim: A policy created through Graph starts disabled.
claims.quote: A new policy is created disabled.

claims.claim: The create body must specify a concrete @odata.type.
claims.quote: Because spendingPolicy is abstract, the request body must set a concrete @odata.type, either #microsoft.graph.allUsersSpendingPolicy or #microsoft.graph.selectedGroupsSpendingPolicy.

claims.claim: The create body requires displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit and serviceSettings.
claims.quote: Required properties are displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and serviceSettings.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; What to check: first bullet
claims.claim: Editing uses Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > policy > Save changes.
claims.quote:
Select the Configuration tab.
Select the spending policy you want to edit.
After making the necessary changes, select Save changes to apply the updates to the spending policy.

claims.claim: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} updates policy name, limits and billing method, not scope, services or alerts.
claims.quote:
PATCH /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}
The following properties can be updated: displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and billingMethods.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls table: changing a policy
claims.claim: Graph updates only displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit and billingMethods.
claims.quote: When billingMethods changes stored funding from non-pay-as-you-go to a value that includes payAsYouGo, including prepaidCredits,payAsYouGo, also supply a billingInstrument
claims.fix: Replace the Graph-update sentence in controls[2].note and its rendered counterpart with: 'Graph updates displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit and billingMethods, with an If-Match ETag header; not scope, services or alerts. When changing non-pay-as-you-go funding to include payAsYouGo, also supply billingInstrument with billingSubscriptionId, billingResourceGroup and billingRegion (a supported billing-geography key, not an arbitrary Azure region).' claims.claim: Updating a policy requires an If-Match header carrying its ETag.
claims.quote: If-Match | The ETag of the spending policy. Required.

claims.claim: The setup page grants AI and License administrators editing of policies, limits, alerts and billing methods but not creation.
claims.quote: AI administrator and License administrator roles can edit spending policies, manage limits and alerts, and billing methods. However, they can't create spending policies.

claims.claim: Alert settings are at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > policy > Alerts, and Email alert settings.
claims.quote:
The spending policy details fly-out opens, where you can modify its settings. This includes:
1. Scope
2. Agents and services
3. Billing method
4. Spending limits
5. Alerts, and Email alert settings

claims.claim: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}/emailThresholdSettings configures policy alerts.
claims.quote: Update costManagementAlertSetting | PATCH /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}/emailThresholdSettings | Create or update the alert configuration.

claims.claim: The Graph alert request body uses isEnabled and thresholds.
Alerts notify rather than stopping consumption.
claims.quote: Configure notify-only threshold alerts and manage their recipients.

claims.claim: Resource policy setup uses Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > Add spending policy > Resources.
claims.quote:
In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost Management.
Select Configuration, and then select Add spending policy.
Enter a name for the policy, then select Resources as its scope.

claims.where: controls[4].api; Governance controls: Watching; Open questions
claims.claim: No Graph or PowerShell operation is documented for resource-based spending policies.
claims.quote: Searched: "resource-based" "spending" "Graph" Copilot API; "resource-based" "spending policy" "API" "PowerShell". Read Studio costs, Graph overview/create and spendingPolicy excerpts; the Graph contract exposes all-users and selected-groups types, not resource policies.

claims.claim: Deleting uses Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > More actions beside the policy > Delete.
claims.quote:
Select the Configuration tab.
From the list of spending policies, locate the spending policy that you want to delete.
Select the More actions menu (⋮) next to the spending policy.
Select Delete.

claims.claim: DELETE https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} deletes a spending policy.
claims.quote: Delete spendingPolicy | DELETE /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} | Delete a spending policy.

claims.claim: Deleting a policy removes its spending limits, not credits or consumption history.
claims.quote:
When you delete a spending policy, the users and groups assigned to that policy are no longer governed by its spending limits.
Deleting a spending policy doesn't remove, reallocate, or reset Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Graph policy creation requires Billing Administrator or Global Administrator at runtime.
claims.quote: At runtime, creating a policy also requires the Billing Administrator or Global Administrator directory role.

claims.claim: AI Reader, Global Reader and supported reader roles can view consumption without changing configuration.
claims.quote: These roles provide read-only access to consumption information and don't allow administrators to create or change spending policies, limits, alerts, request policies, or billing methods.

claims.claim: An existing Power Platform role does not itself become a Microsoft 365 role.
claims.quote: The recommendations are role assignments to consider; an existing Power Platform role does not itself become a Microsoft 365 role.

claims.where: Governance controls: Roles, License Administrator qualification
claims.claim: The setup page inconsistently includes License Administrator among both editors and read-only roles.
claims.quote:
AI administrator and License administrator roles can edit spending policies
AI Reader, Global Reader, License Administrator, and other supported reader-based roles can view consumption dashboards and reports.
These roles provide read-only access

claims.claim: Alert emails start at the configured threshold and repeat daily until reset or policy adjustment.
claims.quote: Alert emails begin when usage reaches the specified threshold and continue daily until the monthly usage period resets or you adjust the spending policy.

claims.claim: After policy deletion users continue under another policy applicable through group membership.
claims.quote: If another spending policy applies to a user through group membership, the user continues to consume Copilot Credits under the applicable policy.

claims.claim: Cost Management's Overview tab refreshes every four hours.
claims.quote: The Overview tab refreshes every 4 hours.

claims.claim: Consumption refreshes every two hours.
claims.quote: The Consumption tab refreshes every 2 hours.

claims.claim: Consumption reports by policy, user, group, agent and service.
claims.quote:
The Consumption tab provides reporting experiences for copilot credit usage by:

- Spending policy
- User
- Group
- Agent
- Service

claims.claim: Consumption includes limit utilisation.
claims.quote: Limit utilization: Credit usage divided by the current spending limit.

claims.claim: Administrators review submitted credit requests on the Credit requests page.
claims.quote: To view and approve credit requests from end users, select View requests. The Credit requests page displays all pending and approved requests.

claims.claim: No spending-policy PowerShell cmdlet is documented in the referenced material.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/powershell "spendingPolicies"; site:learn.microsoft.com/powershell "CopilotCostManagement". Read Graph overview/create/update/list and policy UI pages. Search results exposed REST references, not a spending-policy cmdlet.

claims.claim: The documented 12-minute delay concerns resource policies, not identity-policy limit changes.
claims.quote: Searched: "spending policy" "limit" "change" "immediately" identity; "identity-based" "limit change" spending policy. Read manage-credits, Studio costs and Graph update. Found 12 minutes for environment linking, not identity limit-change latency.
